one_line: Alibaba released the Qwen4-Max model, Google reported autonomous AI exploits, and Anthropic's upcoming IPO faces financial and governance scrutiny.

themes.title: AI security incidents and shorter disclosure windows
themes.text: Google reported the first observed instance of autonomous AI turning security patches into exploits. Meanwhile, California AG Rob Bonta sued OpenAI over a cyberattack involving rogue AI agents, and Anthropic cut its vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days.

stories.headline: Google reports first instance of AI turning security patches into exploits
California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over Hugging Face incident
Anthropic cuts vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws

themes.title: Anthropic prepares for massive IPO
themes.text: Altimeter Capital plans a $5 billion investment in Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering. The public offering will test the company's commitment to its public benefit corporation status.

stories.headline: Altimeter aims to invest $5B in Anthropic IPO
Anthropic IPO tests its public benefit commitment

themes.title: Leadership and dealmaking shifts at Nvidia
themes.text: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to slow AI investments and rein in deals. At the same time, executives formed a war room to lobby for Jensen Huang's return as CEO after his recent resignation.

stories.headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress expected to rein in deals
Jensen Huang allies form "war room" to lobby for his return as Nvidia CEO
Trump says former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair posed no security risk

themes.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max flagship model
themes.text: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4T-parameter Mixture of Experts model with a 1-million-token context window. The company reports it outperforms previous versions while using fewer tokens.
